$doc: The kernel's commands, by number (@xpute/kit/abi/cmd.ts: `major << 8 | minor`),
and the packet each carries — an XTP branch whose children are its fields, in
order. A command with no fields carries no packet. The kernel is the process; the
JavaScript around it is two things to it, its host, which holds the devices and
the turns, and its shell, the UI. The commands are grouped by which of them a
command is between.
The same number is a command on the submission ring and a signal on the
completion ring (its `RES` clear). The direction is the ring: `packet` is
what the shell submits, `signal` what the kernel posts. Each is written and
read by what this file generates, on both sides, so no field is found by
its position anywhere else.
A field is a number of a width, a `bool`, a `str`, a member of an enum
below or of one another spec declares (`extern`), or a record below. An
`optional` one may be absent, its kind kept; a `list` is a branch of them,
or a packed array where the item is a number. A record crosses as a branch
of its own fields, and is how a block past a slot is laid out. An enum's
`unknown` is the member a number it does not give out reads as; an enum
without one refuses the packet. The generator refuses a number given twice.

extern.name: BakeKind
$doc: By its index in BAKE_KINDS (published.spec.ts).

extern.name: SettingKey
$doc: A setting by its place in schema.json's SETTING, its row's `key`.

extern.name: CharacterGroup
$doc: actor.json's group, by its number.

enums.name: Major
$doc: What a command is about.

enums.name: WorldMinor
$doc: The world's verbs.

enums.name: InputMinor
$doc: The input's verbs: the canvas, the pointer, the camera controls.

enums.name: SensorMinor
$doc: The device sensors' verbs.

enums.name: GpuMinor
$doc: The GPU's verbs.

enums.name: SurfaceMinor
$doc: A surface's verbs.

enums.name: SettingMinor
$doc: A setting's verbs.

enums.name: ChatMinor
$doc: The chat's verbs.

enums.name: PreviewMinor
$doc: A preview's verbs.

enums.name: ProfilerMinor
$doc: The profiler's verbs.

enums.name: PointerPhase
$doc: Where a pointer event is in its gesture.

entries.name: Cancel
$doc: The pointer's gesture ends with no tap: the platform took it, or the shell spent it on something of its own.

enums.name: PointerType
$doc: What the pointer is, as the browser's `pointerType` says.

enums.name: ActiveTool
$doc: What the pointer holds.

enums.name: Tracking
$doc: What the tracking button did, as the button showed it.

entries.name: Recenter
$doc: Back to the device.

entries.name: Follow
$doc: Follow mode on, where the compass is listened to.

entries.name: Unfollow
$doc: Follow mode off, north up again.

enums.name: GeolocationErrorCode
$doc: The browser's PositionError codes.

enums.name: Sensor
$doc: Which of the device's sensors.

enums.name: PermissionAnswer
$doc: A sensor permission, as the shell's prompt or the browser's change reported it.

entries.name: Asking
$doc: The shell's prompt is up.

entries.name: Failed
$doc: The prompt itself threw.

enums.name: GroundStatus
$doc: Whether the screen shows the world: Success once a frame that drew ground went
to it, or one went over a view whose tiles all answered with nothing to draw;
Loading until then, on a first load, after a jump or a lost device; Idle before
there is a view.

enums.name: DevicePoseStatus
$doc: Where a sensor's reading is: none asked for, asked for, arriving, failed, or none to be had, the device having no such sensor.

enums.name: Message
$doc: A message the kernel raises and the shell shows.
The kernel decides which message a state calls for and carries the number.
It never carries the words: a string that exists to be read has no reason
to sit in the kernel's memory, and the shell has the locale files already
(ts/client/src/locale) — the same split `strerror` is on the other side of.
The number is the name here, and a band is what a message is about.

entries.section: 0x02 where the device says it is
0x03 which way the device is facing
0x04 why the server does not answer the world's reads

entries.name: WorldReadFailing
$doc: Reads reach the server and fail; they are tried again.

entries.name: WorldUnavailable
$doc: Reads failed past every retry; the world is not coming.

entries.section: the process asks the host: its system calls, raised on the completion ring and run before the next turn (the rest are the host stream's records, host.json)

entries.name: SENSOR_START
$doc: Start watching.

entries.name: SENSOR_STOP
$doc: Stop watching.

entries.section: the host answers: an I/O the process started, done

entries.name: SENSOR_POSITION
$doc: A GPS fix; a field is absent where the browser gave none.

entries.name: SENSOR_ORIENTATION
$doc: An orientation event; a field is absent where the browser gave none.

entries.name: SENSOR_FAILED
$doc: A watch that ended in failure and was stopped, refused from the start (PermissionDenied)
or cut off; the compass's, where the platform says so (WORLD_BOOT's
orientation_silence_is_loss).

packet.name: code
$doc: Geolocation's; orientation gives none today.

entries.section: the host tells the process: its start, its turn, its window, its devices and its input

entries.name: WORLD_BOOT
$doc: The kernel's start: what the platform is. Its kept slots it opens itself, on the storage root.

packet.name: development
$doc: A development build, which offers the settings schema.json marks `dev`.

packet.name: orientation_permission
$doc: iOS 13+'s gate: requestPermission exists and must run inside a gesture.

packet.name: orientation_silence_is_loss
$doc: A browser's compass talks while the device is still and cannot say it stopped, so
silence is the only sign of loss; a device's speaks only when the heading turns and
reports a failure itself (SENSOR_FAILED).

entries.name: WORLD_FRAME
$doc: The frame of the turn the doorbell's quota rang in: the effects' turn, then the tick's
phases on what is left of the quota, the fetches within the credits. The turn leaves
its signals on the completion ring, drawn by the kernel.

packet.name: width
$doc: The viewport, in CSS pixels.

packet.name: refresh_ms
$doc: The display's refresh, as the host measures it from the animation frames it is handed,
and the interval it paces turns at, a whole number of refreshes (xpute host
sched/quantum.ts `Grant`): the frame's budget.

packet.name: unix_ms
$doc: The page's one clock, in Unix milliseconds: the wall time the sky is placed by, and
the step the tick takes, its change since the last frame.

entries.name: WORLD_VISIBILITY
$doc: The tab's visibility; the host rings the doorbell for it at once, since a hidden
page gets no frame and hiding is the save's last sure moment.

entries.name: WORLD_SOURCE
$doc: What the tile source declares of itself, once the client has it: the tile root's
`source`, the published one out of the bucket or the dev tile server's, read by the
client (ts/client/src/namespace/source.ts) and handed over as numbers and names.
Until it comes nothing is observed: the floor is held at the zoom it names, and no
tile is asked for that no shard it serves is over or under (pxl-kernel sys/io/source.rs).

packet.name: top_zoom
$doc: The coarsest zoom the source supplies whole.

packet.name: format
$doc: Each kind's format, one a kind, indexed by its bake's number
(pxl-spec bake/published.spec.rs).

packet.name: shard
$doc: The shards it serves, by name. Their order means nothing: no two at a zoom
are over one node, and the finer wins.

entries.name: WORLD_KEPT_EMPTIED
$doc: A kept slot the kernel refused (the snapshot's `kept_refused`) is empty now, what it held
set aside by the host: the kernel reads it again, and writes it from then on.

packet.name: slot
$doc: host.json's `kept`.

entries.name: SENSOR_PERMISSION
$doc: A permission as the shell's prompt or the browser's change reported it.

entries.name: INPUT_RECT
$doc: The canvas's client rect.

entries.name: INPUT_POINTER
$doc: A pointer event on the canvas, in client pixels.

entries.name: INPUT_HOLD
$doc: What the pointer holds, sent when it changes: the tool, the cube or decor a placing tool takes, and the object size tier. The kernel keeps a cube and a decor apart, so choosing another tool forgets neither, and picks again under a hovering pointer.

packet.name: value
$doc: The held cube or decor kind, by its number in the catalog's one value space (cube.json).

packet.name: tier
$doc: The object size, by its tier: 0 the cell, each next its half (pxl-spec bake/object.spec.rs).

entries.name: INPUT_MARKER_WORDS
$doc: The words the waiting marker (HoldingState.marker) is drawn with and put up with. Words past MARKER_TEXT_CHARS (pxl-spec object/ext.json) are refused whole, never cut.

entries.name: INPUT_MARKER_CANCEL
$doc: The marker the tool left waiting is let go, nothing put up.

entries.name: INPUT_MARKER_PUT
$doc: The waiting marker is put up with its words, if its place is still free or still a marker, and nothing waits after.

entries.name: INPUT_KEYS
$doc: The screen direction the held movement keys point, sent when it changes: each axis -1, 0 or 1, x to the right and y down.

entries.name: GPU_READY
$doc: A device answered: the kernel asks its block (xpute DEVICE) and makes the renderer on it once the block is in (rust/client/render/src/gpu/api.rs). Its loss is the block's to say (xpute STATUS.LOST, written by the host's GpuHost), read at the turn's edge.

entries.section: the shell and the process: what the UI asks of it, and what it shows the UI

entries.name: SURFACE_OPEN
$doc: A call, answered with the surface's handle, 0 refused: a canvas the shell hands over, drawn by the kernel alone from then on.

packet.name: role
$doc: The renderer's surface_role (render/gpu/api.json).

entries.name: SURFACE_RESIZE
$doc: The canvas's layout box in device pixels, transforms aside; the buffer it is drawn into is the kernel's.

entries.name: SURFACE_CLOSE
$doc: A call: the canvas is going, and what it held on the device is let go before the call returns.

entries.name: PREVIEW_OPEN
$doc: A character drawn alone into a surface the shell handed over, as the picker shows it.

entries.name: SETTING_SET
$doc: A setting set from the sheet or the character picker; EAGAIN until the kernel has read the
kept settings, which would be read over it.

packet.name: value
$doc: A toggle's 0 or 1, a choice's option by its index, or a number.

entries.name: CHAT_SEND
$doc: A line the player said, shown over the character.

entries.name: INPUT_TRACKING
$doc: The tracking button's press, as the button showed it.

entries.name: INPUT_COMPASS_RESET
$doc: The compass's press: north up.

entries.name: INPUT_LOCATE
$doc: The search panel's location card's press: the location asked for. The compass is
asked for where it is used, entering follow mode (TRACKING), and never alone: nothing
reads it without the location.

entries.name: INPUT_GO_TO
$doc: A search result: the pivot moved there, and the view asked with it at once, as the
controls ask it where the camera stands; a view field absent keeps what the view has.

packet.name: dist
$doc: The zoom, the eye's distance from the pivot, clamped to the zoom's range; absent, a view far out comes in.

packet.name: azimuth
$doc: The heading about Z in radians, wrapped.

packet.name: polar
$doc: The angle down from vertical in radians, clamped.

entries.name: INPUT_POSE
$doc: A tracked pose: where a tracker has the camera, and its turn as a unit quaternion
(x, y, z, w) from the camera's axes to the tracker's, in the world's units. The
first of a run is taken to be where the camera already is, so nothing moves as
it begins; the camera follows the tracker from there until POSE_END.

entries.name: INPUT_POSE_END
$doc: The tracker let the camera go: back to the controller it had.

entries.name: WORLD_VIEW
$doc: The shell's world view, up or down: the pair of VISIBILITY, whether the page is seen.
The kernel watches a sensor only while both hold, the page visible and the world view
shown; which sensors it watches then is its own (SENSOR_START).

entries.name: PROFILER_START
$doc: A fresh recording window.

entries.name: PROFILER_STOP
$doc: The window frozen, so what is exported holds still.

entries.name: PROFILER_READ
$doc: The profiler's statistics and what it holds now, where they lie: the reply is the address of READ's words (profiler.json), the statistics
over the last `window_ms`, the whole recording where it is absent, good until the next turn. A
number past the door is finite, so no window is infinite.

entries.name: PROFILER_RINGS
$doc: The rings where they lie, nothing reduced: the reply is the address of RINGS's words (profiler.json), good until the next turn.

entries.name: WORLD_SNAPSHOT
$doc: The UI's snapshot, when it changed: a Snapshot packet far past a ring frame, so a
block the kernel holds, valid until the next snapshot.

records.name: Snapshot
$doc: What the page's UI shows of the kernel (shell.rs): written after a turn that changed it, and replaced whole.

fields.name: azimuth
$doc: The view's azimuth.

fields.name: zooming
$doc: A zoom is in hand: two fingers are down, or a wheel's zoom is still arriving. The scale is shown while it is.

fields.name: over_marker
$doc: The pointer is over a marker a tap would act on with the tool held: a place to go to, or a pin to erase or word.

fields.name: settings
$doc: Every setting's value by its SettingKey, as SETTING_SET carries one; none until the kernel
has read its kept slot, a few turns from boot.

fields.name: m_per_px
$doc: The meters a logical pixel spans at the pivot, at the camera's distance; 0 where the camera stands there. The scale bar is the shell's to make of it; which division names show, the kernel's (`DivisionPart.shown`).

fields.name: division
$doc: The division the pivot is in and every one above it, broad to narrow; empty
where the pivot is in none or the tile it is read out of has not arrived.

fields.name: previews
$doc: The surfaces a character preview is drawn on: its model and skin have arrived. The shell shows a case loading until its surface is here.

fields.name: kept_refused
$doc: The kept slots (host.json's `kept`) whose file is not of the slot's format, or too large for
any heap: the kernel read none of it and writes nothing over it until WORLD_KEPT_EMPTIED says
the slot is empty.

fields.name: stall
$doc: Why the server does not answer the world's reads now: failing since the last answered, or given up. Absent while it answers. The network and the GPU are the host's to say.

fields.name: lon_lat
$doc: The pivot in degrees: what the search measures distance from.

fields.name: outside
$doc: The pivot is past the service area: the source serves no shard over it (pxl-kernel sys/io/source.rs).

fields.name: error
$doc: Present exactly when status is Error: the failure the kernel chose.

records.name: HoldingState
$doc: What the pointer holds, as INPUT_HOLD set it: the cube and the decor are each remembered whichever tool is held; and a marker the tool left waiting for its words.

fields.name: cube
$doc: The held cube, by its number in the catalog's one value space.

fields.name: marker
$doc: Whether a marker the tool left waits for its words, which INPUT_MARKER_PUT or INPUT_MARKER_CANCEL ends.

fields.name: words
$doc: The waiting marker's words, which the shell takes up when it starts waiting: the marker's own where one stands there, none where it is new.

fields.name: error
$doc: Present exactly when status is Error: the failure the kernel chose.

records.name: DivisionPart
$doc: One division of the name, in every language the provider had rather than one resolved
name: the reader's language is the page's, and switching it re-reads a label already
sent.

fields.name: subtype
$doc: Overture's subtype, broadest first (spec/spec/division.json).

fields.name: shown
$doc: The view is in far enough for its name to show: as far as Overture's own tiles
show it from (pxl-spec bake/tile/division.rs `Division::shown_from`).

fields.name: area
$doc: Held by an area the point is in; one without is the nearest found by its point.
